column11: derived and found to be nil: AbbVie generated $17,816mm of free cash flow on $61,160mm of revenue in FY2025, a 29.13% margin, against the 28.95% its cost of sales, SG&A and R&D leave. The two reconcile to within a fifth of a point, which is why this is zero rather than absent: the check was run and it found nothing to charge. Restated before interest: ABBV paid $3,002mm of interest inside operating cash flow over 2025, 4.91% of revenue. The free cash flow above is struck after it and the valuation already charges the debt by subtracting net debt, so adding it back only widens a gap the filed lines already leave, and the charge stays nil. Restated at replacement capex: ABBV spent $1,214mm on plant over 2025 against $762mm of plant depreciation, 0.74% of revenue above what keeps the plant running. Taken at depreciation, the charge stays nil. Checked without one-off cash: deal payments are booked under investing, so free cash flow never carried them, and no settlement or transition tax is stated for the window, so the charge stands. Restated to the amortisation floor: the filed cost lines leave a 32.46% pre-tax margin where the cash over 2025 supports 38.40%, so the charge rebuilds at -5.94%. It was held at nil, but ABBV books $7,377mm of non-cash amortisation of acquired intangibles inside cost of sales in FY2025 (0001551152-26-000008), 12.06% of revenue, so the charge takes the rebuilt figure: -5.94%.
column12: AbbVie books its amortisation of acquired intangibles inside cost of sales, $7,377mm of it, which is why its 29.8% cost of sales is so far above Pfizer's 25.7% and why the same test that charged Pfizer 22% charges AbbVie nothing. The older windows would imply a credit, not a cost: 33.6% over three years and 36.3% over five, both above the model, because they carry peak Humira.
